service timestamps debug datetime msec localtime show-timezone

no ip http server
no ip http secure-server
username lab-breakglass privilege 15 secret 0 <REDACTED>
enable secret 0 <REDACTED>
aaa new-model

tacacs server TAC-LOCAL
 address ipv4 10.10.99.12
 timeout 3
 key 0 <REDACTED>

tacacs server TAC-REMOTE
 address ipv4 10.20.99.12
 timeout 3
 key 0 <REDACTED>

aaa group server tacacs+ TAC-GROUP
 server name TAC-LOCAL
 server name TAC-REMOTE

ip tacacs source-interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1.199
aaa authentication login default group TAC-GROUP local
aaa authentication login CONSOLE local
aaa authorization exec default group TAC-GROUP local
aaa authorization commands 15 default group TAC-GROUP local
aaa accounting exec default start-stop group TAC-GROUP
aaa accounting commands 15 default start-stop group TAC-GROUP

ip access-list standard ADMIN-SOURCES
 permit 10.10.99.0 0.0.0.255
 permit 10.20.99.0 0.0.0.255
 deny any log

ip access-list standard SNMP-MANAGERS
 permit host 10.10.99.11
 permit host 10.20.99.11
 deny any log

logging buffered 65536 informational
logging trap informational
logging source-interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1.199
logging host 10.10.99.10 transport udp port 514
logging host 10.20.99.10 transport udp port 514
snmp-server view NMS-READ iso included
snmp-server group NMS-GROUP v3 priv read NMS-READ access SNMP-MANAGERS
snmp-server user nms-reader NMS-GROUP v3 auth sha <REDACTED> priv aes 128 <REDACTED>

ntp server 10.20.99.13
ip ssh version 2
ip ssh time-out 60
ip ssh authentication-retries 3
! Provision RSA host keys separately: crypto key generate rsa modulus 2048
banner motd ^CAtlas Retail fictional training lab. Authorized lab access only.^C

line con 0
 login authentication CONSOLE
 exec-timeout 15 0
 logging synchronous

line vty 0 15
 access-class ADMIN-SOURCES in
 login authentication default
 authorization exec default
 authorization commands 15 default
 accounting exec default
 accounting commands 15 default
 transport input ssh
 exec-timeout 10 0

ip routing
track 10 interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0 line-protocol

interface Loopback0
 description BGP-ROUTER-ID
 ip address 10.255.10.1 255.255.255.255

interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0
 description WAN-A TO LON-R01 Gi0/0/0 VIA CARRIER

 no ip redirects
 no ip proxy-arp
 bfd interval 300 min_rx 300 multiplier 3
 no bfd echo
 no shutdown

interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1
 description 802.1Q TRUNK TO DXB-SW01 Gi1/0/1
 no ip address
 no shutdown

interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1.110
 description USERS-VRRP-GATEWAY
 encapsulation dot1Q 110
 ip address 10.10.10.2 255.255.255.0
 no ip redirects
 no ip proxy-arp
 vrrp 110 ip 10.10.10.1
 vrrp 110 priority 120
 vrrp 110 preempt delay minimum 30
 vrrp 110 timers advertise 1
 vrrp 110 track 10 decrement 40

interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1.199
 description MANAGEMENT-VRRP-GATEWAY

 ip address 10.10.99.2 255.255.255.0
 no ip redirects
 no ip proxy-arp

 vrrp 199 priority 120
 vrrp 199 preempt delay minimum 30
 vrrp 199 timers advertise 1
 vrrp 199 track 10 decrement 40

 description ROUTED-IBGP TO DXB-R02 Gi0/0/2

 no ip redirects
 no ip proxy-arp
 bfd interval 300 min_rx 300 multiplier 3
 no bfd echo
 no shutdown

interface GigabitEthernet0/0/3
 description UNUSED
 shutdown

interface range TenGigabitEthernet0/0/4 - 5
 description UNUSED-SFP-PLUS-NO-OPTIC-INSTALLED
 shutdown

ip prefix-list LOCAL-SITE seq 10 permit 10.10.10.0/24
ip prefix-list LOCAL-SITE seq 20 permit 10.10.99.0/24
ip prefix-list LOCAL-SITE seq 30 permit 10.255.10.1/32
ip prefix-list LOCAL-SITE seq 40 permit 10.255.10.2/32

ip prefix-list REMOTE-SITE seq 10 permit 10.20.20.0/24
ip prefix-list REMOTE-SITE seq 20 permit 10.20.99.0/24
ip prefix-list REMOTE-SITE seq 30 permit 10.255.20.1/32
ip prefix-list REMOTE-SITE seq 40 permit 10.255.20.2/32

ip prefix-list IBGP-ALLOWED seq 10 permit 10.10.10.0/24
ip prefix-list IBGP-ALLOWED seq 20 permit 10.10.99.0/24
ip prefix-list IBGP-ALLOWED seq 30 permit 10.255.10.1/32
ip prefix-list IBGP-ALLOWED seq 40 permit 10.255.10.2/32

ip prefix-list IBGP-ALLOWED seq 60 permit 10.20.99.0/24
ip prefix-list IBGP-ALLOWED seq 70 permit 10.255.20.1/32
ip prefix-list IBGP-ALLOWED seq 80 permit 10.255.20.2/32

route-map WAN-IN permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list REMOTE-SITE
 set local-preference 200

router bgp 65010
 bgp router-id 10.255.10.1
 bgp log-neighbor-changes
 no bgp default ipv4-unicast
 neighbor 10.0.0.2 remote-as 65020
 neighbor 10.0.0.2 description EBGP-WAN-A
 neighbor 10.0.0.2 timers 10 30
 neighbor 10.0.0.2 fall-over bfd
 neighbor 10.10.254.2 remote-as 65010
 neighbor 10.10.254.2 description IBGP-SITE-PEER
 neighbor 10.10.254.2 timers 10 30
 neighbor 10.10.254.2 fall-over bfd
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 10.10.10.0 mask 255.255.255.0
  network 10.10.99.0 mask 255.255.255.0
  network 10.255.10.1 mask 255.255.255.255
  neighbor 10.0.0.2 activate
  neighbor 10.0.0.2 prefix-list REMOTE-SITE in
  neighbor 10.0.0.2 prefix-list LOCAL-SITE out
  neighbor 10.0.0.2 route-map WAN-IN in
  neighbor 10.0.0.2 maximum-prefix 4 80 restart 5
  neighbor 10.10.254.2 activate
  neighbor 10.10.254.2 next-hop-self
  neighbor 10.10.254.2 prefix-list IBGP-ALLOWED in
  neighbor 10.10.254.2 prefix-list IBGP-ALLOWED out
 exit-address-family

1. WAN-A silent loss while Ethernet remains up
BFD on both WAN-A endpoints should fail near 900 ms under negotiated 300x3 conditions. eBGP is withdrawn; R02's WAN-B route becomes preferred and is shared to R01 over direct iBGP. R01 can remain VRRP master and forward to R02. This depends on route propagation/FIB update, so measure end-to-end loss rather than asserting 900-ms restoration.

page_content:
1. Scope
Two sites: Dubai (DXB), AS 65010; London (LON), AS 65020. Each site has two C8300 routers and two independent C9200L switches: eight network devices total. IOS XE 17.12.x is a target syntax family, not a certification of an exact release. Two independent 1-Gbps carrier Ethernet circuits provide WAN-A (R01 to R01) and WAN-B (R02 to R02). Carrier physical diversity is a design assumption requiring real procurement evidence.

metadata.document_context:

page_content:
2. LAN and gateways
Each router connects by one 802.1Q trunk to its corresponding switch. Switches share a two-member LACP port channel. User and management VLANs span both switches at that site. VRRP on routers supplies a .1 virtual gateway per subnet; R01 and R02 use .2 and .3. R01 has priority 120; R02 100. Switches perform Layer 2 forwarding only. No cross-chassis EtherChannel, stacking, or multichassis LAG is assumed.

metadata.document_context:

page_content:
3. WAN routing
Direct eBGP on each WAN uses BFD. A dedicated routed interrouter link runs direct iBGP with BFD and next-hop-self. WAN-A-learned remote routes receive local preference 200, WAN-B routes 150. The preferred normal intersite path is WAN-A from both routers at both sites. On failure, existing alternative paths can use WAN-B; VRRP gateway movement is not required for every WAN failure. Exact prefix filters limit advertisements to the documented site user and management networks and router loopbacks. There is no default route, Internet edge, NAT, DHCP server, or IPv6 in this lab.

page_content:
4. Management
Each site has a syslog receiver, SNMPv3 manager, TACACS+ server, and NTP server in its management VLAN. All network devices use their unique management address as the service source, not the VRRP VIP. Remote-site service destinations supplement local services. Servers are individually single-attached to SW01; remote-site services improve continuity but do not create server clustering or recover local logs that were never delivered.

page_content:
1. Addressing and physical links
devices.csv, links.csv, addressing.csv and services.csv enumerate every modeled device, connection, routed address, VIP, and server. DXB users: 10.10.10.0/24 VLAN 110; management: 10.10.99.0/24 VLAN 199. LON users: 10.20.20.0/24 VLAN 120; management: 10.20.99.0/24 VLAN 299. Gateways are .1 (VRRP), routers .2/.3, switches management .21/.22. DXB router IDs: 10.255.10.1/.2; LON: 10.255.20.1/.2 (all /32).
WAN-A 10.0.0.0/30: DXB-R01 .1, LON-R01 .2. WAN-B 10.0.0.4/30: DXB-R02 .5, LON-R02 .6. Site iBGP transit: DXB 10.10.254.0/30, LON 10.20.254.0/30, R01 .1 and R02 .2. Transit networks are not exported through BGP.
Router Gi0/0/0 is WAN, Gi0/0/1 is the LAN trunk, Gi0/0/2 the direct iBGP link, Gi0/0/3 unused. Each switch Gi1/0/1 faces its router, Gi1/0/2 and /3 form Port-channel1, /4-/8 are user access, /9-/12 on SW01 serve LOG/NMS/AAA/NTP respectively. Corresponding server ports on SW02 are reserved and shut. /13-/24 and Te1/1/1-/4 are shut. Endpoint devices use static addresses in the demo.

page_content:
2. BFD and BGP
Every router has interface command bfd interval 300 min_rx 300 multiplier 3 on WAN and interrouter interfaces, no bfd echo, and neighbor fall-over bfd on its eBGP and iBGP peers. Asynchronous control packets are used; routed paths must pass BFD single-hop UDP 3784 and TCP 179. With matching negotiated 300-ms intervals and multiplier 3, expected BFD detection is about 900 ms, not a guaranteed total traffic recovery time. This moderate lab starting value trades detection speed against scheduling/jitter sensitivity. Validate CPU, packet loss, carrier treatment, and actual negotiated timers; relax to e.g. 1000 ms x 3 on a lab image that cannot sustain 300 ms. BGP keepalive/hold 10/30 seconds remains a fallback where BFD is unavailable; no strict-mode or graceful-restart helper behavior is explicitly configured. Verify inherited defaults before measuring.
Inbound eBGP route-map WAN-IN applies local preference 200 on R01, 150 on R02. LOCAL-SITE allows exactly the local user /24, management /24, and two local loopbacks /32. REMOTE-SITE allows the equivalent four remote prefixes. iBGP uses next-hop-self and permits the eight documented site prefixes. Both directions have explicit filters. Maximum-prefix 4 on each eBGP neighbor is appropriate only for this fixed corpus and must be revised if prefixes are added.

page_content:
3. VRRP
IPv4 VRRPv2 syntax is used. User groups: DXB 110, LON 120. Management groups: DXB 199, LON 99 (group numbers are independent of VLAN numbers and must fit 1..255). VIP .1 is not a physical router IP. R01 priority 120, R02 100; both decrement by 40 when their own WAN physical line protocol fails. R01 uses preempt delay minimum 30 to avoid immediate failback; R02 preempts without that delay. Advertisement interval is 1 second. Backup master-down estimate at priority 100: 3 + (256-100)/256 = 3.609 seconds. Startup, priority-change, platform scheduling, ARP and forwarding updates affect observed recovery.
Tracking is physical WAN line protocol ONLY. A silent carrier or BGP-only failure does not automatically lower VRRP priority. In that case BFD/BGP and the direct interrouter path provide routing recovery. BFD is not directly attached to VRRP in this design. If the interrouter path and one WAN fail together, gateway reachability can fail despite local link-up tracking; this is a documented compound-failure limitation.

page_content:
4. Layer 2
Rapid-PVST is configured with SW01 priority 24576, SW02 28672. Both interswitch links belong to the same ordinary LACP bundle. Native VLAN 999 is unused and excluded from the trunk allowed list; all service VLAN traffic is tagged. Router-facing switch ports have no PortFast; user/server access ports have PortFast and BPDU Guard. There is no BFD on this Layer 2 port channel: LACP/physical state detects its member failure. Management VLAN 299 is valid even though VRRP group 299 would not be.

5. Platform and credentials
Router target C8300-1N1S-4T2X, autonomous IOS XE; switch target C9200L-24T-4X, independent units with member number 1. Interfaces and features require exact image/license confirmation. All modeled data ports are copper RJ45; there are no CE SFPs. Provider transport optics, serial numbers and bill of materials are unknown. Every <REDACTED> value hides a credential field. Bootstrap RSA keys separately with crypto key generate rsa modulus 2048 after hostname/domain provisioning; persistent key material is not represented by a text config. Boot variables, licenses, certificates, default/hidden commands and platform management-port defaults are outside the generated baseline. No actual configurations have been pushed to hardware.

Device configuration sends informational-and-higher messages to both receivers on UDP 514 and maintains a 65536-byte local buffer. Receiver must bind/listen on UDP 514, allow the eight device management IPs, retain timestamps and source identity, and store/rotate messages per hostname. Transport has neither TLS nor delivery acknowledgement. This is a teaching baseline; no receiver daemon has been deployed.

page_content:
3. SNMP
Managers poll the eight unique management IPs using SNMPv3 authPriv, username nms-reader, SHA authentication and AES-128 privacy, with secrets matching substituted device placeholders. Polling uses UDP 161 on devices and traps UDP 162 on managers. Device ACL allows only 10.10.99.11 and 10.20.99.11. NMS-READ is a read-only view of iso; no SNMP write view or v1/v2c community is configured. Configure trap receiver engine/user handling for each sender on the selected NMS. SNMP user secrets may not appear in show running-config; inspect show snmp user separately. A manager application, polling schedule and MIB inventory are not installed by these files.

page_content:
4. TACACS+
Each device references local and remote TACACS+ servers, timeout 3 seconds per configured server, source unique management IP, TCP 49. In the server, register all eight device management IPs with their matching device-relative key. DXB device TACACS_LOCAL must match DXB AAA server and TACACS_REMOTE must match LON; reverse this for LON devices. Prefer unique per-device keys when implementing. Configure an authorized lab-admin identity, shell privilege 15, command authorization for intended lab commands and accounting retention. Server software selection, identity-store integration and server-specific policy syntax are not supplied. Never interpret local fallback as bypassing an explicit TACACS denial. <REDACTED> is the console/break-glass placeholder; test via console before enabling remote AAA in a lab.

5. NTP and access
Provide actual time service on each .13 server; devices prefer the local one and can use the remote. UTC timestamps support correlation. Management SSH access is limited to the two management subnets. These ACLs are service restrictions, not a complete management security boundary: routed interfaces do not have a comprehensive infrastructure ACL, control-plane policy or management VRF. Platform defaults, crypto policy and server-side firewalls require validation for a deployment. Client endpoints use static addresses; no DHCP/DNS application is included.

WAN ports: Gi0/0/0. BFD 300ms x3 on both WANs AND direct iBGP links.
Normal route preference: WAN-A local-pref 200; WAN-B 150.
VRRP: R01 priority 120, R02 100; physical WAN-down decrement 40.
VRRP advertisements 1s; R01 preempt delay 30s; R02 no preempt delay.
Each router has user/mgmt address .2 (R01) or .3 (R02).
Each switch has mgmt .21 (SW01) or .22 (SW02).
Po1 uses switch Gi1/0/2 AND Gi1/0/3 at both ends.

SERVERS AT EACH SITE (all attached to SW01 management access ports):
  Gi1/0/9  -> LOG01 .10   UDP 514
  Gi1/0/10 -> NMS01 .11   UDP 161 polls / 162 traps
  Gi1/0/11 -> AAA01 .12   TCP 49 TACACS+
  Gi1/0/12 -> NTP01 .13   UDP 123
  Server subnet: 10.10.99.0/24 DXB, 10.20.99.0/24 LON; gateway .1.

All CE links are copper RJ45. Provider optics unknown, not invented.
Servers are single-attached. Loss of ALL Po1 members partitions site VLANs.
